title: Personality
note: Personality is a person's long-standing pattern of thinking, feeling and behaving. Freud stressed unconscious conflict, humanists stressed growth and the self, social-cognitive theorists stressed thought, behavior and setting acting on one another, and trait theorists measure stable dimensions. The best-supported trait model today is the Big Five.

read.title: Five traits that travel well
text: If you list every English word that describes a person, you get thousands: kind, moody, punctual, bold, curious. Gordon Allport and his colleagues did exactly that. The lexical hypothesis holds that the most important ways people differ will be captured in everyday language.

Researchers then used statistics to find which words cluster together. People who are called punctual also tend to be called organized and hardworking. After decades of such work, five broad dimensions kept appearing, now known as the Big Five: openness to experience, conscientiousness, extroversion, agreeableness and neuroticism, remembered as OCEAN.

Each trait is a continuum, not a box. Most people fall near the middle on most traits, and five scores describe a person far better than a single type label. The five factors appear in many cultures, and they matter in daily life; conscientiousness, for example, predicts success in school and work.

Traits are not destiny. In 1968 Walter Mischel pointed out that behavior varies a lot from one situation to the next. Later work found that both matter: traits predict how a person acts on average across many situations, while the situation shapes what they do in any single moment.
